# dggev

> Computes generalized eigenvalues and eigenvectors for a pair of real nonsymmetric matrices.

<section class="usage">

## Usage

```js
import dggev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dggev';
```

### Layout API

Takes a storage layout (`order`) and leading dimensions, like CBLAS/LAPACKE.

```js
dggev(
    order,
    jobvl, jobvr,
    N,
    A, LDA,
    B, LDB,
    ALPHAR, strideALPHAR,
    ALPHAI, strideALPHAI,
    BETA, strideBETA,
    VL, LDVL,
    VR, LDVR,
    work
) → info: integer
```

Computes the generalized eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right.
generalized eigenvectors for a pair of N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrices (A,B).

When `work` is `null`, this LAPACKE-style wrapper allocates the optimal
workspace, `max( 8*N, 7*N + N*NB + TSIZE )` elements, as a convenience.
Prefer passing a caller-owned buffer for batched use.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `order` | `Layout` | Storage layout ('row-major' or 'column-major') |
| `jobvl` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` to compute left eigenvectors, `'no-vectors'` to not |
| `jobvr` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` to compute right eigenvectors, `'no-vectors'` to not |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix A (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `LDA` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of A<br>Requires `LDA ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix B (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `LDB` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of B<br>Requires `LDB ≥ max(1, N)` |
| `ALPHAR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: real parts of alpha (length N) |
| ↳ `strideALPHAR` | `integer` | Stride length for `ALPHAR` |
| `ALPHAI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: imaginary parts of alpha (length N) |
| ↳ `strideALPHAI` | `integer` | Stride length for `ALPHAI` |
| `BETA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: beta values (length N) |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | Stride length for `BETA` |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: left eigenvectors (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDVL` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of VL<br>Rejects `ldvl < 1 \|\| ((jobvl === 'compute-vectors') && ldvl < N)` |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: right eigenvectors (N x N) |
| ↳ `LDVR` | `PositiveInteger` | Leading dimension of VR<br>Rejects `ldvr < 1 \|\| ((jobvr === 'compute-vectors') && ldvr < N)` |
| `work` | `Float64Array \| null`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 8 * N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,8*N)`; for optimal performance at least `max( 8*N, 7*N + N*NB + TSIZE )` (`NB` from `ilaenv`, `TSIZE = 4160`), the reference's `N*(7+NB)` with the dormqr optimum's T part, which enables the blocked QR steps; or `null` to allocate the optimal size<br>Optional, default `null`. |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvl`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the left generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the left generalized eigenvectors.
- `jobvr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the right generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the right generalized eigenvectors.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A, B, `VL`, and `VR`. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the matrix A in the pair (A,B). On exit, A has been overwritten.
- `B`: On entry, the matrix B in the pair (A,B). On exit, B has been overwritten.
- `BETA`: On exit, (`ALPHAR(j)` + `ALPHAI(j)`\*i)/`BETA(j)`, $j=1$,...,N, will be the generalized eigenvalues. If `ALPHAI(j)` is zero, then the j-th eigenvalue is real; if positive, then the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues are a complex conjugate pair, with `ALPHAI(j+1)` negative.

  Note: the quotients `ALPHAR(j)`/`BETA(j)` and `ALPHAI(j)`/`BETA(j)` may easily over- or underflow, and `BETA(j)` may even be zero. Thus, the user should avoid naively computing the ratio $\alpha$/$\beta$. However, `ALPHAR` and `ALPHAI` will be always less than and usually comparable with norm(A) in magnitude, and `BETA` always less than and usually comparable with norm(B).
- `VL`: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$ and $u(j+1) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part)+abs(imag. part)=1. Not referenced if `JOBVL = 'N'`.
- `VR`: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part)+abs(imag. part)=1. Not referenced if `JOBVR = 'N'`.
- `work`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, 1..N if QZ iteration failed, N+1 for other errors

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be a valid order
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` third argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `RangeError` fourth argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` sixth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` eighth argument must be greater than or equal to `max( 1, N )`
- `RangeError` sixteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVL < 1 \|\| ( ( jobvl === "compute-vectors" ) && LDVL < N )`)
- `RangeError` eighteenth argument is invalid (rejected when `LDVR < 1 \|\| ( ( jobvr === "compute-vectors" ) && LDVR < N )`)
- `RangeError` LDA must be >= max(1,N)
- `RangeError` LDB must be >= max(1,N)

### Strided (ndarray) API

Takes explicit strides and offsets for every array. Use it for views, sub-matrices and non-unit strides.

```js
dggev.ndarray(
    jobvl, jobvr,
    N,
    A, strideA1, strideA2, offsetA,
    B, strideB1, strideB2, offsetB,
    ALPHAR, strideALPHAR, offsetALPHAR,
    ALPHAI, strideALPHAI, offsetALPHAI,
    BETA, strideBETA, offsetBETA,
    VL, strideVL1, strideVL2, offsetVL,
    VR, strideVR1, strideVR2, offsetVR,
    WORK, strideWork, offsetWork
) → info: integer
```

Computes the generalized eigenvalues and, optionally, the left and/or right.
generalized eigenvectors for a pair of N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrices (A,B).

Matrix shapes are logical (rows × columns). The reference's leading dimension (`LDA`, …) is replaced by the two strides and the offset.

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `jobvl` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` to compute left eigenvectors, `'no-vectors'` to not |
| `jobvr` | `"no-vectors" \| "compute-vectors"` | `'compute-vectors'` to compute right eigenvectors, `'no-vectors'` to not |
| `N` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Order of matrices A and B<br>Requires `N ≥ 0` |
| `A` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix A (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `strideA1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of A |
| ↳ `strideA2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of A |
| ↳ `offsetA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for A |
| `B` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **in/out** · Input matrix B (N x N), overwritten on exit |
| ↳ `strideB1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of B |
| ↳ `strideB2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of B |
| ↳ `offsetB` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for B |
| `ALPHAR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: real parts of alpha (length N) |
| ↳ `strideALPHAR` | `integer` | Stride for ALPHAR |
| ↳ `offsetALPHAR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for ALPHAR |
| `ALPHAI` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: imaginary parts of alpha (length N) |
| ↳ `strideALPHAI` | `integer` | Stride for ALPHAI |
| ↳ `offsetALPHAI` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for ALPHAI |
| `BETA` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length N</sub> | **out** · Output: beta values (length N) |
| ↳ `strideBETA` | `integer` | Stride for BETA |
| ↳ `offsetBETA` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for BETA |
| `VL` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: left eigenvectors (N x N) |
| ↳ `strideVL1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of VL |
| ↳ `strideVL2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of VL |
| ↳ `offsetVL` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for VL |
| `VR` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>N × N</sub> | **out** · Output: right eigenvectors (N x N) |
| ↳ `strideVR1` | `integer` | First dimension stride of VR |
| ↳ `strideVR2` | `integer` | Second dimension stride of VR |
| ↳ `offsetVR` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Offset for VR |
| `WORK` | `Float64Array`<br><sub>length ≥ max(1, 8 * N)</sub> | **out** · Workspace of length at least `max(1,8*N)`; for optimal performance at least `max( 8*N, 7*N + N*NB + TSIZE )` (`NB` from `ilaenv`, `TSIZE = 4160`), the reference's `N*(7+NB)` with the dormqr optimum's T part, which enables the blocked QR steps |
| ↳ `strideWork` | `integer` | Stride for WORK |
| ↳ `offsetWork` | `NonNegativeInteger` | Starting index for WORK |

<details>
<summary>Reference notes for each argument (the reference implementation's own documentation; 1-based indices)</summary>

- `jobvl`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the left generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the left generalized eigenvectors.
- `jobvr`:

  -   `= 'N'`: do not compute the right generalized eigenvectors;
  -   `= 'V'`: compute the right generalized eigenvectors.
- `N`: The order of the matrices A, B, `VL`, and `VR`. $N \ge 0$.
- `A`: On entry, the matrix A in the pair (A,B). On exit, A has been overwritten.
- `B`: On entry, the matrix B in the pair (A,B). On exit, B has been overwritten.
- `BETA`: On exit, (`ALPHAR(j)` + `ALPHAI(j)`\*i)/`BETA(j)`, $j=1$,...,N, will be the generalized eigenvalues. If `ALPHAI(j)` is zero, then the j-th eigenvalue is real; if positive, then the j-th and (j+1)-st eigenvalues are a complex conjugate pair, with `ALPHAI(j+1)` negative.

  Note: the quotients `ALPHAR(j)`/`BETA(j)` and `ALPHAI(j)`/`BETA(j)` may easily over- or underflow, and `BETA(j)` may even be zero. Thus, the user should avoid naively computing the ratio $\alpha$/$\beta$. However, `ALPHAR` and `ALPHAI` will be always less than and usually comparable with norm(A) in magnitude, and `BETA` always less than and usually comparable with norm(B).
- `VL`: If `JOBVL = 'V'`, the left eigenvectors u(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VL`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VL`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $u(j) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$ and $u(j+1) = \mathrm{VL}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VL}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part)+abs(imag. part)=1. Not referenced if `JOBVL = 'N'`.
- `VR`: If `JOBVR = 'V'`, the right eigenvectors v(j) are stored one after another in the columns of `VR`, in the same order as their eigenvalues. If the j-th eigenvalue is real, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)$, the j-th column of `VR`. If the j-th and (j+1)-th eigenvalues form a complex conjugate pair, then $v(j) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)+i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$ and $v(j+1) = \mathrm{VR}(:,j)-i \, \mathrm{VR}(:,j+1)$. Each eigenvector is scaled so the largest component has abs(real part)+abs(imag. part)=1. Not referenced if `JOBVR = 'N'`.
- `WORK`: On exit, if `INFO = 0`, `WORK(1)` returns the optimal `LWORK`.

</details>

**Returns** `info: integer`: 0 on success, 1..N if QZ iteration failed, N+1 for other errors

**Throws**

- `TypeError` first argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `TypeError` second argument must be one of the following: "no-vectors", "compute-vectors"
- `RangeError` third argument must be a nonnegative integer
- `RangeError` work array must have sufficient length

### Status codes

An `info` status code: `0` on success. A positive value reports a numerical condition such as a singular pivot or a failure to converge (see the description). Invalid arguments throw instead of returning a negative `info`. Returns immediately when `N === 0`.

The reference documents `INFO` as:

-   `= 0`: successful exit
-   `< 0`: if `INFO = -i`, the i-th argument had an illegal value.
-   `= 1,...,N`:  The QZ iteration failed.  No eigenvectors have been calculated, but `ALPHAR(j)`, `ALPHAI(j)`, and `BETA(j)` should be correct for $j=\mathrm{INFO}+1$,...,N.
-   `> N`: =N+1: other than QZ iteration failed in DHGEQZ. =N+2: error return from DTGEVC.

<section class="notes">

## Notes

-   `dggev()` corresponds to the reference LAPACK routine [`DGGEV`](https://github.com/Reference-LAPACK/lapack/blob/v3.12.0/SRC/dggev.f).
-   The generalized eigenvalues are returned as the pairs (ALPHAR(j)+i*ALPHAI(j), BETA(j)), j=1,...,N. The eigenvalue is ALPHAR(j)/BETA(j) + i*ALPHAI(j)/BETA(j) when BETA(j) is nonzero.
-   Workspace is allocated internally; there is no LWORK parameter.

</section>

<!-- /.notes -->

<section class="examples">

## Examples

```js
import Float64Array from '@stdlib/array/float64/lib/index.js';
import dggev from '@rreusser/blahpack/lapack/base/dggev';

// Compute generalized eigenvalues of a 3x3 matrix pair (A, B):
const N = 3;

// Column-major matrices:
const A = new Float64Array( [ 1, 4, 7, 2, 5, 8, 3, 6, 10 ] );
const B = new Float64Array( [ 1, 0, 0, 0, 2, 0, 0, 0, 3 ] );

const ALPHAR = new Float64Array( N );
const ALPHAI = new Float64Array( N );
const BETA = new Float64Array( N );
const VL = new Float64Array( 1 );
const VR = new Float64Array( N * N );

const info = dggev( 'column-major', 'no-vectors', 'compute-vectors', N, A, N, B, N, ALPHAR, 1, ALPHAI, 1, BETA, 1, VL, 1, VR, N, null );

console.log( 'info:', info ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
console.log( 'eigenvalues (alphar/beta):', ALPHAR[ 0 ] / BETA[ 0 ], ALPHAR[ 1 ] / BETA[ 1 ], ALPHAR[ 2 ] / BETA[ 2 ] ); // eslint-disable-line no-console
```

</section>

<section class="reference-notes">

## Reference notes

The mathematical description from the reference LAPACK 3.12.0 source of `DGGEV`. Indices are the 1-based Fortran indices of the source.

### Purpose

DGGEV computes for a pair of N-by-N real nonsymmetric matrices (A,B) the generalized eigenvalues, and optionally, the left and/or right generalized eigenvectors.

A generalized eigenvalue for a pair of matrices (A,B) is a scalar $\lambda$ or a ratio $\alpha /\beta = \lambda$, such that $A - \lambda \, B$ is singular. It is usually represented as the pair ($\alpha$,$\beta$), as there is a reasonable interpretation for $\beta =0$, and even for both being zero.

The right eigenvector v(j) corresponding to the eigenvalue lambda(j) of (A,B) satisfies

$$
A \, v(j) = \lambda (j) \, B \, v(j)
$$

The left eigenvector u(j) corresponding to the eigenvalue lambda(j) of (A,B) satisfies

$$
u(j)^H \, A = \lambda (j) \, u(j)^H \, B
$$

where $u(j)^H$ is the conjugate-transpose of u(j).

</section>
